sources.title: Polymarket unit gets US industry organization's approval to be futures broker
Congo opens mining fraud inquiry after copper and cobalt seizures, statement shows
Shell to sell North West Shelf stake to XRG for $1.45 billion

stories.headline: Polymarket unit approved by NFA to be futures broker
stories.body: The US National Futures Association approved Polymarket unit PM Derivatives LLC as a futures commission merchant. US CFTC authorisation remains required before it can act as a broker. The firm intends to run fully collateralised positions.
stories.analysis: Regulatory progress, but licensing and protection of customer funds remain unresolved.
stories.watch_next: Watch CFTC authorisation, actual operational start and customer-fund safeguards.

stories.headline: Congo opens mining fraud probe following copper and cobalt seizures
stories.body: DR Congo ordered investigations into suspected mining fraud and smuggling following seizure of more than 500 trucks and thousands of metric tons of copper and cobalt. Authorities separately reported over 500 pieces of equipment seized at an ERG-owned site and more than 60 foreign nationals detained. Allegations remain under investigation.
stories.analysis: Critical minerals supply-chain compliance risk; no global shortage confirmed.
stories.watch_next: Watch formal findings, production disruptions and metals-supply effects.

stories.headline: Shell agrees to sell North West Shelf LNG stake to XRG
stories.body: Shell agreed to sell its 16.67% non-operated North West Shelf LNG interest to ADNOC subsidiary XRG for US$1.45 billion base consideration, with possible milestone-linked payments. The buyer assumes decommissioning obligations; closing is expected in 2027.
stories.analysis: LNG asset rotation; project liabilities and contingent terms matter.
stories.watch_next: Watch transaction approvals, contingent payments, decommissioning liabilities and actual LNG flows.
